title: Normal charts and regular boundary equation on a full SNC root limit
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, $k$ a field of characteristic $p$, $Y$ a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme], and $B=\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ an affine etale chart. Let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in A$, $r\geq0$, be branch equations of a reduced strict normal crossings divisor on $B$, whose branches are precisely $V(t_d)$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Let $A\to R$ be weakly etale, meaning that this ring map and $R\otimes_A R\to R$ are flat [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Write
$$S=\varinjlim_{n\geq1,\ (n,p)=1}R[x_{1,n},\ldots,x_{r,n}]/(x_{d,n}^n-t_d)_{1\leq d\leq r},$$
with transition $x_{d,n}\mapsto x_{d,m}^{m/n}$ for $n\mid m$, using polynomial rings [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and ring colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For every weakly etale $S$-algebra $Q$, the ring $Q$ is normal [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]: each prime localization $Q_{\mathfrak q}$ is a domain integrally closed in its fraction field. Moreover multiplication by the image $s\in Q$ of $t_1\cdots t_r$ is injective on $Q$. The zero algebra $Q$ and empty chart are allowed. For $r=0$, the product is $1$ and $S=R$.

proof.text: Use étale ascent of regular stalks and local Noetherianity to obtain regularity of Spec A from hY. The existing source theorem isRegularLocalRing_stalk_of_etale and the Mathlib LocallyOfFiniteType instance give this in two lines. In boundary_regular, the effective Cartier ideal clause, the product-ideal equality and the proved affine-generator theorem give injectivity of multiplication by the product on A. The radical clause gives radicality of its principal ideal. In boundary_equations, write the product as t_i*d and cancel d to show that each (t_i) is radical. If two zero loci agree, their radical principal ideals agree; writing t_j=t_i*c makes the product t_i^2*c*d. Radicality forces t_i*c*d into the product ideal; cancellation makes t_i a unit, contradicting the nonempty irreducible-component condition. Thus the branch equations are reduced and distinct as required by the finite-root theorem.
